catalog.commands.summary: The registry listing (toolportctl commands): every command with its tier and a search, Run for the read-only ones and Copy for the rest; a form per command arrives with the first command that needs operands

catalog.mcp-call.summary: Run a self-management tool through mcp call with its arguments as JSON on stdin, a preview when the tool offers one, the tool name typed to confirm for a tool that changes things

system.doctor.summary: Installation checks, including whether this build carries the fork seam (doctor)

system.mcp-doctor.summary: Check the self-management server and where it is listed (mcp doctor)

system.mcp-install.summary: Register the self-management server and list it in an access set (mcp install)

system.mcp-tools.summary: List the self-management tools and resources (mcp tools)

system.mcp-uninstall.summary: Remove the self-management server and keep it removed (mcp uninstall)

system.status.summary: Registry, access sets, secrets backend and gateway state (status)

servers.list.summary: The servers list: every server with its global switch and the default access (server ls, servers_list); upstream's list stays whole, the fork adds banner rows

servers.detail.summary: One server's Operations rows: command, plain env keys, access sets and what its process sees of the shell environment (server info, servers_get)

servers.add-catalog.summary: Add a curated catalog server and finish its setup: secrets, who can reach it (server install)

servers.add.summary: Add a server from a command or a URL, with plain env and the shell-environment switch, then Finish setup (server new, servers_install)

servers.edit.summary: Edit a server's command, arguments, URL, plain env and the shell-environment switch through upstream's Edit; the Runtime row explains what the process sees (server edit, servers_update_config)

servers.remove.summary: Remove a server and its vault entries, with a preview first (server uninstall, servers_uninstall)

servers.restart.summary: Restart a server in every running gateway: one click when idle, a confirmation naming the calls in flight otherwise, a result per gateway with retry (server restart, servers_restart)

servers.access-sets.summary: Servers by access set in one table (servers_list_profiles)

servers.access-set-member.summary: List a server in an access set or take it out: a table cell with Undo, the Finish setup chips, the Reach row (servers_add_profile_tag, servers_remove_profile_tag)

servers.advanced-mode.summary: Per server, whether its tools are listed to clients that get the full tool list (auto) or only found through toolport_search_tools and called by name (search), in the Advanced disclosure; the screen row comes later (server mode, servers_set_mode)

servers.secret-set.summary: Set or replace a secret of a server, or the access token of a remote one, through a write-only field in upstream's Secrets dialog; the value goes to stdin only, a placeholder is refused (secret set)

servers.secret-reveal.summary: Say which declared keys of a server are set, and reveal one after a confirmation; it hides after 10 seconds and the access token is never shown (secret get)

servers.secret-remove.summary: Remove a secret and its declaration after a confirmation, typed when the policy tier is destructive (secret rm)

servers.login.summary: Sign in to a server again from its Login row: a remote server through the Sign in button's flow, a stdio or Google server through its own auth command with the consent link shown (auth login, servers_auth)

servers.login-check.summary: Check now on the Login row of a stdio or Google server, with the state, its reason and when it was last checked; remote servers have no Login row (auth probe)

servers.login-summary.summary: The login summary line for a statusline or a session hook, counting stdio and Google logins only; no client is wired to it (auth statusline, auth hook)

context.bundles.summary: Folder bundles: list, show, create (from a folder too), edit and delete a bundle definition (context bundle ls|show|add|edit|rm, context_bundle_ls)

context.bundle-apply.summary: Apply a bundle to a folder after its plan, drift per key, undo, copy the launch command and the auto-apply switch (context bundle apply|undo|status|launch|config, context_bundle_apply|undo|status)

context.use.summary: Apply a bundle and route the folder to its access set, or drop both (context use)

context.leave-out.summary: Leave a CLAUDE.md or rule out of a folder, or turn auto memory off, one click with Undo (context leave-out, context_leave_out)
